analysis.title: Entegris Inc. (ENTG): Execution continues to improve, with cyclical recovery driving upside to wafer starts and CapEx estimates
key_insights: GS expects ENTG to trade higher after a strong 3Q26 print and outlook, against elevated investor expectations. Positioning was constructive going in on a CapEx upcycle, strong 2Q results and improving utilization in memory and logic.

Management now expects wafer starts to grow 8% in 2026 (up from 7%-8% prior), driven by advanced nodes and improvement in mainstream logic. Similar growth is expected in 2027, with a preliminary view of mid-to-high single digits.
3Q26 revenue was $1,006mn vs GS $931mn and Street (Visible Alpha) $926mn. Gross margin was 48.9% vs GS 48.2% and Street 48.1%. Non-GAAP operating EPS was $1.23 vs GS $1.04 and Street $1.03.
Segment results: Materials Solutions revenue $404mn vs GS $388mn and Street $387.9mn. Advanced Purity Solutions revenue $605mn vs GS $545mn and Street $543.2mn.

Gross margin expanded about 530bps y/y on better yield, productivity and utilization of new facilities. Taiwan reached breakeven this quarter, Colorado is operational and producing samples, and exits continue in Utah, Arizona and Pennsylvania.

4Q26 guidance is above the Street. Revenue midpoint is $1,040mn vs GS $968mn and Street $964mn. EPS range is $1.32-$1.40 (midpoint $1.36) vs GS $1.16 and Street $1.13. Gross margin midpoint is 49.5% vs 48.5% for both GS and Street. Adjusted EBITDA margin is about 31% vs GS 25.6% and Street 29.5%.
Management guided 1Q27 down mid-single digits Q/Q.
On CapEx, Entegris expects continued improvement through 2026 and more meaningful acceleration in 2027 as greenfield fabs come online.
Net leverage ended 3Q at 2.9x, with a target below 2.7x by end of 2026. The multi-year CapEx investment cycle is complete, with CY26 CapEx tracking to $200mn vs about $300mn in CY25.
GS raised CY26-28 EPS estimates by an average of 13%. 2026E EPS goes to $4.43 from $4.00, 2027E to $5.75 from $5.10, and 2028E to $6.70 from $5.85.

GS raised its price target to $135 from $120, based on 30x P/E (unchanged) on normalized EPS of $4.50 (up from $4.00). The stock is Sell-rated, with 15.3% downside from the $159.32 close on 28 Oct 2026.

GS stays Sell on ENTG while it awaits clearer signs of a sustained upturn in fab construction-related business. It prefers Qnity (Buy) for stronger revenue growth and margins, citing advanced packaging, substrates and thermal management.
GS sees a positive read-across to Qnity (Buy) from management's constructive commentary on 2026 and 2027 wafer starts.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target from $120 on higher revenue and margin assumptions, but the target still implies 15.3% downside from $159.32 (17.4% in the exhibit). GS expects Entegris fundamentals to lag peers.
GS sees a positive read-across from ENTG's wafer start commentary and prefers Qnity on revenue growth and margin profile. Pricing in the disclosures shows Qnity at $122.79.

sector_views.rationale: Wafer starts are expected to accelerate in 2027, but GS wants clearer signs of a sustained upturn in fab construction-related business before turning positive on ENTG.

earnings_insights: ENTG 3Q26 revenue reported $1,006mn vs GS est $931mn and Street (Visible Alpha) consensus est $926mn. Revenue was +13.9% Q/Q and +24.6% y/y.

ENTG 3Q26 non-GAAP diluted EPS reported $1.23 vs GS est $1.04 and Street consensus est $1.03. Non-GAAP gross margin reported 48.9% and non-GAAP operating margin 26.8% (GS est 25.0%, Street est 25.1%).

ENTG 4Q26 guidance: revenue midpoint $1,040mn (range $1,025-$1,055mn) vs prior GS est $968mn and Street consensus est $964mn. Non-GAAP EPS guidance $1.32-$1.40 vs GS est $1.16 and Street est $1.13. Non-GAAP gross margin guided to 49.5% at midpoint vs 48.5% GS and Street est. Adjusted EBITDA margin guided to about 31% vs GS est 25.6% and Street est 29.5%.
ENTG 1Q27 is guided down mid-single digits Q/Q.

GS estimates (new vs old): 2026E revenue $3,752mn vs $3,594mn, 2027E $4,290mn vs $4,080mn, 2028E $4,684mn vs $4,405mn. Non-GAAP EPS 2026E $4.43 vs $4.00, 2027E $5.75 vs $5.10, 2028E $6.70 vs $5.85. These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.

macro_indicators.reading: +8% in 2026 (up from +7% to +8% prior); similar growth in 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: This is management's outlook. Higher content per wafer from logic and memory node transitions supports materials demand.

macro_indicators.indicator: Global wafer starts growth, 2027 preliminary view
macro_indicators.interpretation: Management's preliminary view points to continued cyclical recovery, with greater CapEx acceleration as greenfield fabs come online.

risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell rating: (1) better-than-expected recovery in wafer starts and fab construction-related CapEx in 2026; (2) faster qualification and uptake of new products such as molybdenum at advanced nodes; (3) rapid deleveraging with strong FCF.
GS expects ENTG fundamentals to lag peers, including Qnity, until a sustained upturn in fab construction-related business appears.
Net leverage of 2.9x remains above the sub-2.7x target for end of 2026.
vol_and_positioning: GS says investor positioning was constructive heading into the print, with expectations for a CapEx upcycle, strong 2Q results and improving memory and logic utilization.
GS says expectations were elevated going into the print, and still expects the stock to trade higher after the results and outlook.

tension_points.bear_case: GS stays Sell, expecting ENTG fundamentals to lag peers like Qnity, and wants clearer signs of a sustained upturn in fab construction-related business. The price target of $135 sits below the $159.32 price.
